title: Hedgehog pathway
subject: Conceptual cell signaling from a membrane receptor toward a nucleus
alt: Blue cutaway cell with a surface receptor and a signaling relay leading toward the nucleus.
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational editorial illustration.
Asset type: the FIRST Hedgehog pathway glossary hero for RemapRx, to sit in a small left-hand blue hero panel, consistent with existing soft blue anatomy illustrations.
Create one original compact conceptual illustration of cellular signaling: a single round cell shown in a clean cutaway, with a clearly defined curved outer cell membrane, one simple receptor shape embedded at the upper-left membrane, and a small group of three rounded signaling protein shapes forming a gentle visual route toward a clearly visible round nucleus inside the cell. Show a small extracellular signal near the receptor. Keep the nucleus inside the cell. Make this a conceptual image of membrane-to-nucleus signaling, not a complete molecular pathway map, not a claim about a drug. Do not represent particular proteins, exact molecular shapes, activation states or a numbered reaction sequence.
Style: quiet medical editorial artwork, simple rounded silhouettes, broad smooth tonal planes, softly modeled but nearly flat, no photographic texture. A clear large silhouette readable at 200 pixels wide. Restrained blue palette #8FA4FF #C5D0FF #E2E8FF #5674E8 #3455C8. Mid-blue cell body, pale-blue membranes, pale nucleus and small light-blue signal nodes; separate forms clearly. Designed to be readable against a deep royal-blue #1027B8 page background.
Composition: one centered isolated subject on a square canvas, generous even transparent margin around all sides (at least12percent). Avoid clutter, tiny organelles and decorative specks.
Absolutely no text, letters, labels, numerals, logos, arrows, hedgehog animal, drug tablets, yellow accents, shadows on a floor, background panels, gradients in the background or watermarks. Real transparent background outside the illustration.
scope: Conceptual editorial illustration; not a complete molecular pathway or exact protein structure.
